description:
FILED s540 (the reviewing session, 2026-11-13) at the s539d merge review (probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s540/review/e/p1.pl + .perl / .main / .tree / .treelt).

TODAY (MAIN-READY-92): the frame's file id / line slots are filled from the location registers, which only PCL_OPT=line-track updates (recording by default was measured and left out: +4-6 % on counting loops, +17.9 % emitted text).  So the default build answers `caller` -> (pkg, "-", 0) and Carp prints `bad thing at - line 0.`; perl: `bad thing at p1.pl line 18.`.  `die "x"` is right in both builds (its location is a compile-time constant at the die site).

THE CHEAP HALF: the file of frame N's call site is the file of the code that MADE the call -- the sub of frame N+1 (every named sub is compiled from one file: a per-SUB constant, recorded once at definition beside its name), or for a call from top level the unit being run (the main script, or the module file being loaded: the loader knows it).  Nothing is stored per call; `caller` looks it up from the frame it already has.  Exceptions to measure: a sub defined by a string eval (perl: `(eval N)`), a sub installed by glob assignment from another file (the file of its DEFINITION is still right), `# line` directives (the per-sub constant must be the directive's file), AUTOLOAD / goto &sub frames.

THE LINE stays 0 without line-track.  QUESTION TO MEASURE, not to assume: is `at FILE line 0.` more useful than `at - line 0.`?  (the reviewing session thinks yes: the file is the half a reader acts on; a test matching `/ at \S+ line \d+/` passes either way.)  A cheaper line approximation (the calling SUB's definition line) is NOT wanted: it is a wrong positive number.

ALSO from the probe: Carp's backtrace lines read `main::thrower called at` where perl prints `main::thrower() called at` (no : print the empty parens) and the `eval {...} called at` line is missing (eval frames: tier 2).

BAR: the frame's cost rows unchanged (the s539d bench method: fib, subret, methret, emptysub, anoncall inside the band), Pl/t/caller-fidelity-01.t rows for a module sub called from the main program and the reverse, the everyday program `carp-attribution` re-read.  Size: under one session.
subject: `caller` / `croak` in the DEFAULT build say file `-` and line 0 (`msg at - line 0.`): the FILE of a call site is known with NO per-call cost -- it is the file the CALLING sub (or the main program / the module being loaded) was compiled from; only the LINE needs line-track
